subject: Adding 30 seats + Premium tier — what's the path?
body:
Priya — quick one. We've decided to push Northwind across the agent-onboarding team. That's +30 seats. Also want SSO so I'd like Premium tier. What's the easiest paperwork path?

Robin

subject: Re: Adding 30 seats + Premium tier — what's the path?
body:
Robin — easiest path is a mid-cycle amendment. Sending paper today. Math: 30 seats x current rate + Premium delta = ~$31k incremental. Effective immediately on countersign, prorated through Feb renewal.

Will you be at Northwind Connect (our user conference) in October? Lena and I want to invite you to do a 20-min talk on Initech's adoption story. No prep beyond what you'd say to a peer. Lots of prospects in the room would benefit.

— P

subject: Re: Adding 30 seats + Premium tier — what's the path?
body:
Yes to the talk. Send me whatever framing you want.

Robin

subject: Renewal — we're not renewing
body:
Priya — wanted to give you the heads-up directly rather than have you hear from procurement. We've decided not to renew Northwind for the May cycle. We're going with [vertical-specific competitor] — they have native integrations with the corporate-travel platforms we use that we'd otherwise have to build ourselves on top of Northwind.

This isn't about Northwind's product. You've been excellent. It's about fit-to-stack for corporate travel specifically.

Happy to do a debrief call if useful for your team.

Lia

subject: Rekall — churning May. Loss-driver: vertical integration depth
body:
Lena, Diego, Marcus —

Flagging early so we can avoid surprise. Rekall is not renewing. Lia (VP Ops) gave me direct heads-up. Loss-driver is corporate-travel platform integrations — competitor has native, we'd need custom builds.

Not a product-quality issue. It's fit-to-stack in a vertical we don't serve well. Will write up a full loss report with Lia's debrief inputs.

Diego — this is the third corporate-travel-vertical loss in 18 months (Vandelay tried us and didn't expand, Macrohard had similar challenges in the EMEA tier). Worth a roadmap conversation about whether we're avoiding that vertical or investing.

— P

title: Loss report: Rekall Travel ($95k ARR, churned May 2025)
author: Priya Sharma
body:
## Summary
Rekall Travel did not renew. ARR loss: $95k. Cause: vertical-specific competitor with native corporate-travel platform integrations. Confirmed via debrief call with Lia Sandoval (VP Ops).

## Account history
- Won 2023-05. Initial use case: agent itinerary workflow + expense exception routing.
- Strong adoption in Year 1 (75% seat utilization).
- Q3 2024 onward: usage flat. Reason in retrospect: their stack was evolving toward corporate-travel-specific tools and Northwind became one workflow tool among several.

## What we did
- Q4 2024 QBR: introduced potential expansion paths. Did not land.
- Q1 2025: Hannah ran a feature-gap session, identified 4 integrations they'd want. Diego scoped 2 of them.
- Q1 2025: Marcus and I built the renewal proposal with a 10% discount.

## Loss-driver
Direct quote from Lia: 'You're a great horizontal tool. We've moved to a vertical world. The integrations our team needs ship in our competitor's box. I'd need three quarters of custom development on top of Northwind to match what they offer Day 1.'

This is not recoverable in a single product cycle. The competitor has 3 years of vertical-specific investment.

## What we'd recommend differently
1. **Earlier vertical-fit signal-tracking.** We had usage data showing flatline in Q3 2024. We didn't connect that to vertical-fit; we read it as adoption work-needed. Need a CSM-side flag for 'usage flat with no resolvable cause' that triggers vertical review.
2. **Loss inventory by vertical.** This is the third corporate-travel vertical loss. We should formally inventory and share with Diego/Product as a roadmap signal.
3. **No discount-to-rescue when fit is the issue.** A 10% discount won't beat a structural fit gap. We chose it as a try-anything; it confused our internal narrative about whether the loss was about price.

## Action for Diego (Product)
Decide explicitly: do we invest in corporate-travel vertical, or do we write off the segment? Either is acceptable. Drift is not.

## Handover note
Rekall's contacts are warm — Lia would take a call again if we re-enter the vertical credibly. Don't burn the relationship.
